tracks.title: Wind Chime
tracks.mood: a grief you have no standing to feel
tracks.subject: the neighbour's wind chime you resented for fourteen years and now miss
tracks.caption: American slowcore built around pedal steel. Pedal steel playing long weeping swells with audible bar movement, baritone electric guitar striking single clean notes and letting them ring out fully, brushed snare keeping a bare pulse, upright bass played soft and slow, one tremolo guitar note under the final chorus. Extremely sparse and slow with long decays and deliberate silence between phrases, nothing filling the gaps. Low male voice, almost spoken, recorded very close with breath left in, no vibrato and no belting. 62 BPM, C major. A grief you have no standing to feel. No drum kit fills, no synth, no strings section, no chorus lift, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - pedal steel and brushed snare]

[Verse 1]
Fourteen years that thing hung on her porch
Cheap aluminum, four tubes, one of them too short
I counted every night I couldn't sleep through it
I had a whole speech ready. Never gave it.

[Chorus]
Now the hook is still there and nothing's on it
And I stand at my window like an idiot, waiting
I didn't know I had memorized it
I didn't know it was the sound of somebody being home

[Verse 2]
Her son came with a truck on a Tuesday
Took the chairs, the pots, the chime. The hook stayed.
He waved at me. I waved back. That's the most we ever did.
Fourteen years of a sound and I never learned her last name

[Chorus]
Now the hook is still there and nothing's on it
And I stand at my window like an idiot, listening
I didn't know I had memorized it
I didn't know it was the sound of somebody being home

[Bridge - pedal steel alone]
I bought one. Hung it on my own porch.
Wrong pitch. Course it is.

[Outro - pedal steel, fading]
Four tubes, one of them too short
I'll leave it up

tracks.title: Recipe Card
tracks.mood: tender, slightly comic, unresolved
tracks.subject: learning your late mother's handwriting from her recipe cards
tracks.caption: Chamber pop led by a Wurlitzer electric piano. Wurlitzer with its natural reed bark and tremolo carrying the main figure, a home upright piano doubling it an octave up, a small string quartet entering under the second chorus, vintage drum kit played with brushes and mic'd minimally with one overhead and a kick mic, round electric bass. Warm, narrow and analogue-saturated, drums close and dry rather than roomy. Warm female voice, conversational and lightly worn, very little processing on it. 88 BPM, F major. Tender and slightly comic, and it does not resolve. No synth pad, no programmed drums, no big belted climax, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Wurlitzer and upright piano]

[Verse 1]
Index card, grease spot on the corner, blue ink gone brown
"Oven hot. Don't open it. You'll know."
That is the whole instruction. That is the whole recipe.
She wrote it for herself. She never wrote it for me.

[Pre-Chorus]
Her sevens have a line through them
Her g's don't close

[Chorus]
I'm learning my mother's handwriting at thirty-eight
Like a language I heard my whole life and never spoke
Every card is a sentence she only had to half-finish
Because she was always going to be there to say the rest

[Verse 2]
There's one that just says "the good pan"
I do not know which one is the good pan
I have eleven pans and I have tried nine of them
I am not going to find it, and I am going to keep trying

[Chorus - strings enter]
I'm learning my mother's handwriting at thirty-eight
Like a language I heard my whole life and never spoke
Every card is a sentence she only had to half-finish
Because she was always going to be there to say the rest to me

[Outro - Wurlitzer, fading]
Oven hot. Don't open it.
I'll know.

tracks.title: Mall Walkers
tracks.mood: unexpectedly held
tracks.subject: walking laps of a shopping mall at seven in the morning with retirees
tracks.caption: Downtempo synth R&B. Deep sustained sub bass, a wide shimmering pad from a vintage-style polysynth with two slightly detuned sawtooth oscillators through a key-tracked low-pass filter, finger snaps and soft rimshots instead of a kit, muted electric piano chords, one filtered vocal sample looping. Wide and hazy with a heavy low end under a bright airy top, long reverb on the pads and a dry close lead. Breathy male voice with wide stacked harmony on the chorus, relaxed and behind the beat. 74 BPM, D flat major. Unexpectedly held by strangers. No trap hi-hat rolls, no rap verse, no live drum kit, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - sub bass and shimmer pad]

[Verse 1]
Seven in the morning, doors open before the stores do
Terrazzo floor, one lap is a quarter mile, there's a sign that says so
Nine of them in windbreakers, same loop, same order every day
And me, thirty-one, in last night's shirt

[Chorus]
Mall walkers
They have been doing this since before I could drive
Gloria has had two knees replaced and she laps me
Nobody here asks what I do for a living

[Verse 2]
Frank brings the coffee. Bad coffee. Everybody takes it.
They have opinions about the fountain. Strong ones.
I came because my gym closed and I didn't want to go home
I stayed because somebody said "you're back" on the fourth day

[Chorus]
Mall walkers
They have been doing this since before I could drive
Gloria has had two knees replaced and she still laps me
Nobody here has ever once asked what I do for a living

[Bridge - pad only]
The stores open at ten and we scatter
Like we weren't anything

[Outro - sub bass, fading]
Quarter mile. Sign says so.
Tomorrow, seven.

tracks.title: They Spell It With A C
tracks.mood: comic fury at yourself
tracks.subject: ten years of never correcting the spelling of your own name
tracks.caption: Electroclash disco pop. Hard-edged distorted analog synth arpeggio running the whole track, four-on-the-floor kick with a tight dry snare, octave-jumping synth bass, short disco string stabs, clavinet scratching on the offbeats. Loud, dry and mid-forward with deliberately abrasive synth tone and very little reverb. Female voice, deadpan and clipped in the verses, shouted and doubled on the chorus with no autotune. 124 BPM, A minor. Comic fury directed entirely at yourself. No ballad section, no live drums, no rap, no big reverb wash, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - distorted arpeggio and four-on-the-floor]

[Verse 1]
Ten years of cups with somebody else's name on them
Close enough that I never said anything
I take the cup, I say thanks, I drink it
I have built an entire adult life on not correcting people

[Pre-Chorus]
It's four letters. It is four letters.
I could fix it in one second and I never do

[Chorus]
They spell it with a C
And I answer to it, I turn around, I smile
Somewhere there's a version of me who said it the first time
I would like to meet her. I think she's taller.

[Verse 2]
New girl at the counter asked me twice, actually asked
She said "how do you really spell that"
I told her. She wrote it right. She said it back right.
I sat in my car for a minute. Thirty-four years old.

[Chorus]
They spell it with a C
And I answer to it, I turn around, I smile
Somewhere there's a version of me who said it the first time
I would like to meet her. I think she's louder.

[Outro - synths cut]
Cup says the right thing today
I'm keeping it. That's insane. I'm keeping it.
[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: Jury Summons
tracks.mood: wry, then quietly moved
tracks.subject: being called for jury duty and wanting to be picked
tracks.caption: Plugg rap. Detuned bell and music-box melody looping softly, a very wide washed-out pad behind it, sparse rounded 808 with no aggressive glide, light scattered hi-hats that drop out for whole bars, no snare on most of the beat. Dreamy and minimal with huge empty space and everything slightly blurred and quiet. Male rap voice, low and conversational, unhurried, lightly doubled with no autotune melody. 138 BPM, E minor. Wry, then quietly moved. No hard trap drums, no shouting, no sung chorus, no bright lead synth.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - detuned bells and pad]

[Verse 1]
Envelope says "official business, do not discard"
I discarded two before this one, that's a crime I think
Room four-oh-two, hard chair, no outlets, they take your phone
A hundred and nine strangers learning each other's coughs

[Hook]
Jury summons
First time in my life the government wanted me specifically
Thirty dollars a day and a sandwich
And I sat up straighter than I have all year

[Verse 2]
Lawyer asked me do I believe people can change
I said yes before I thought about it
Then I thought about it for the next six hours
They didn't pick me. I wanted to be picked. Didn't know that till they didn't.

[Hook]
Jury summons
First time in my life the government wanted me specifically
Thirty dollars a day and a sandwich
And I sat up straighter than I had all year

[Bridge - bells only]
Walked out at four and everybody scattered
Hundred and nine people I will never see again
Knew their coughs though

[Outro - pad fades]
Envelope's on my fridge
Do not discard

tracks.title: Setrika Seragam
tracks.mood: doing the one thing you can actually fix
tracks.subject: ironing a child's school uniform at nine every night
tracks.caption: Indonesian soft rock ballad. Clean electric guitar with long chorused sustain playing arpeggios and one melodic solo, grand piano underneath, fretless bass sliding between notes, drum kit played softly with the ride cymbal open, a string pad entering only in the last chorus. Polished and wide with generous reverb on the guitar and a close dry vocal. Male voice, warm and restrained, staying in a comfortable register and lifting only on the final line. 82 BPM, B flat major. Doing the one thing you can actually fix. No programmed drums, no kendang, no autotune, no rap, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - clean electric guitar and piano]

[Verse 1]
Jam sembilan malam, anaknya sudah tidur
Seragam putih, kerahnya agak kuning, aku setrika pelan di bagian itu
Namanya dijahit di dada, benang merah, jahitan aku sendiri
Jelek. Tapi dia belum pernah komplain.

[Pre-Chorus]
Besok dia pakai, besoknya kotor lagi
Setiap malam aku mulai dari awal lagi

[Chorus]
Aku setrika seragam
Bukan karena harus rapi
Tapi karena besok pagi ada satu hal di hidup dia yang pasti beres
Dan malam ini, itu yang bisa aku kasih

[Verse 2]
Dia pernah bilang temannya ketawa karena sepatunya
Aku diam, aku cuma bilang "besok kita lihat"
Sepatunya belum ganti, tapi seragamnya paling rapi di kelas
Aku tahu itu bukan jawabannya. Aku tetap setrika.

[Chorus]
Aku setrika seragam
Bukan karena harus rapi
Tapi karena besok pagi ada satu hal di hidup dia yang pasti beres
Dan malam ini, itu masih yang bisa aku kasih

[Outro - guitar, fading]
Gantung di pintu
Jam enam dia bangun

tracks.caption: Sundanese-influenced Indonesian pop. Kacapi zither plucked dry and close with its bright metallic decay carrying the harmonic bed, suling bamboo flute floating above it with the characteristic breathy slides and ornaments, a soft frame drum keeping a light pulse instead of a kit, upright bass very soft underneath, one sustained bowed note under the last chorus. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no synth, no belting, no key change.

回してる 回ってる
百年前からこの町は これを回してる

모일 이유가 하나는 있어야 해서

tracks.mood: strangers made equal by weather
tracks.subject: twenty motorcyclists waiting out the rain under a flyover
tracks.caption: Malaysian dikir barat adapted to pop. Rebana frame drums driving an interlocking pattern, maracas shaking on the offbeats, heavy group handclaps and thigh-slap body percussion, one low gong marking the section changes, and almost no harmonic instruments at all. Dry and percussive with the voices stacked very wide and the drums close. A single male lead caller delivering each line and a large seated group answering him in unison, call and response throughout, shouted rather than polished. 112 BPM, D minor pentatonic. Strangers made equal by weather. No guitars, no keyboard, no synth, no drum kit, no key change.

tracks.mood: small renovation standing in for a big one
tracks.subject: repainting one living room wall the same white two weeks before the festival
tracks.caption: Malaysian zapin fused with electronic production. Gambus lute playing the traditional zapin melodic figure, a set of marwas hand drums keeping the characteristic interlocking zapin rhythm, accordion holding sustained chords, and under them a modern deep sub bass and a short plucked synth doubling the gambus. The acoustic zapin layer is recorded dry and close while the low end is clean and modern underneath it. Male and female voices trading lines in the verses and joining in unison on the chorus. 118 BPM, A minor. A small renovation standing in for a big one. No drum kit, no distorted guitar, no autotune, no EDM riser, no key change.

tracks.mood: thirty years of listening and one night of being heard
tracks.subject: a father who listened to a midnight radio request show for thirty years and never called in
tracks.caption: Taiwanese Hokkien folk rock with pipa as the lead instrument. Pipa playing fast tremolo and sharp plucked attacks as the main melodic voice set against the band, large hand cymbals and small bells adding metallic accents inside the kit, steel-string acoustic guitar strummed steadily, drum kit and electric bass driving underneath. tracks.subject: a refrigerator that only rattles sometimes, and a mother who pays for the repair
tracks.caption: Thai post-punk. tracks.subject: forty minutes stopped on an expressway, and the phone call it bought you
tracks.caption: Thai string band pop in the 1990s band idiom. Two jangly electric guitars with light chorus playing interlocking arpeggios and spread wide, drum kit with a roomy gated snare and open hi-hats, round warm bass, a Hammond-style organ pad underneath, a short clean guitar solo. Roomy nineties band sound with real reverb on the drums and the guitars wide rather than modern and dry. Male voice, plain and mid-range, unhurried and slightly nasal, backing harmony on the chorus. 108 BPM, C major. Permission to be still. No synth lead, no programmed drums, no autotune, no rap, no key change.

tracks.title: ร้านซักผ้าหยอดเหรียญ
tracks.genre: Thai luk krung retro big band
tracks.mood: three strangers with nothing to be
tracks.subject: a coin laundry at half past ten and a man who folds very slowly
tracks.caption: Thai luk krung in the retro dance-band idiom. Full brass section with trumpets and trombones playing soft cushioned figures, drums swinging on the ride with brushes, double bass walking, hollow-body archtop guitar comping four to the bar, clarinet obbligato answering the voice. Warm retro dance-band sound with a dark ribbon-microphone character and natural hall reverb. Female voice with classic luk krung phrasing, clear diction and light controlled vibrato on line endings, elegant rather than belted. 92 BPM, F major. Three strangers with nothing they need to be. No synth, no programmed drums, no electric bass, no mor lam elements, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - brass and swing drums]

[Verse 1]
สี่ทุ่มครึ่ง ร้านซักผ้าหยอดเหรียญ มีฉันกับอีกสองคน
ไม่มีใครคุยกัน ทุกคนดูเครื่องของตัวเอง หมุนเหมือนกันหมด
ผู้ชายคนนึงพับผ้าเก่งมาก เก่งจนฉันแอบดู
เขาพับเสื้อเด็ก ทีละตัว ช้ามาก

[Chorus]
ร้านซักผ้าหยอดเหรียญ
สี่สิบนาที ไม่มีใครที่นี่ต้องเป็นใคร
เราแค่คนสามคนที่รอของตัวเองแห้ง
และนั่นคือสิ่งเดียวที่เราต้องทำในโลกนี้ตอนนี้

[Verse 2]
เครื่องฉันหยุดก่อน ฉันเก็บผ้า ฉันพับแบบลวก ๆ
ผู้ชายคนนั้นมองมา ไม่ได้ว่าอะไร แค่มอง
ฉันพับใหม่ ฉันพับช้าลง ฉันไม่รู้ว่าทำไม
ออกจากร้าน ผ้าฉันเรียบที่สุดในปีนี้

[Chorus]
ร้านซักผ้าหยอดเหรียญ
สี่สิบนาที ไม่มีใครที่นี่ต้องเป็นใคร
เราแค่คนสามคนที่รอของตัวเองแห้ง
และคืนนี้ แค่นั้นก็พอแล้วจริง ๆ

[Outro - brass, fading]
เหรียญสิบ สี่เหรียญ
พรุ่งนี้ฉันเตรียมไว้แล้ว

tracks.title: ครูสอนพิเศษ
tracks.mood: gratitude that arrives after the person leaves
tracks.subject: a twenty-three-year-old tutor who explains the same thing four times
tracks.caption: Thai phleng phuea chiwit folk rock. Harmonica carrying the main motif, two steel-string acoustic guitars strummed hard and recorded with their natural rasp, electric slide guitar answering in the gaps, electric bass simple and root-driven, a plain drum kit with no fills, a little tambourine in the choruses. Unpolished and direct with the guitars strummed hard and the mix left slightly rough. Male voice, rough and plain-spoken, delivering lines like speech with a worn grain. 100 BPM, G major. Gratitude that arrives after the person has gone. No synth, no programmed drums, no autotune, no horn section, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - harmonica and acoustic guitar]

[Verse 1]
ครูมาทุกวันอังคาร หกโมง ขี่มอเตอร์ไซค์ ถือถุงหนังสือ
ครูอายุยี่สิบสาม ครูยังเรียนอยู่ ครูสอนเพื่อจ่ายค่าเทอมตัวเอง

[Chorus]
ครูสอนพิเศษ
ครูไม่ได้สอนฉันแค่เลข ครูสอนฉันว่าคนเหนื่อยหน้าตาเป็นยังไง
ครูง่วงจนตาแดง แต่ครูอธิบายซ้ำได้สี่รอบ
ฉันจำเลขไม่ได้ แต่ฉันจำสี่รอบนั้นได้

[Verse 2]
ปีนี้ครูเรียนจบ ครูไม่มาแล้ว ครูไปทำงานที่อื่น

[Outro - harmonica, fading]

tracks.subject: two hours of evening cram school nobody is actually studying in
tracks.caption: Vietnamese math rock. Two clean electric guitars played with two-handed tapping in shifting odd meters, bright and chiming with no distortion, drum kit playing across the bar line with heavy ghost notes on the snare, melodic bass moving independently rather than following the guitars, glockenspiel doubling the guitar figure in the bridge. Bright and dry with every instrument clearly separated and almost no reverb. Young male voice, clipped and syllable-dense, fitting words against an uneven pulse, half-spoken. 148 BPM, A major. The thing you were actually there for. No distortion, no synth, no autotune, no big chorus lift, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - tapped clean guitars]

[Verse 1]
Bảy giờ tối, lớp học thêm trên tầng ba, quạt trần quay chậm
Ba mươi đứa, ba mươi cái lưng cong, không đứa nào muốn ở đây

Lớp học thêm buổi tối

Tám rưỡi nghỉ giữa giờ, cả lớp xuống dưới mua bánh tráng

[Chorus]

Không ai học, nhưng ai cũng có mặt

[Outro - guitars stop]
Chín giờ rưỡi, ba mươi chiếc xe đạp
Ra khỏi cổng cùng một lúc

tracks.title: cái quạt trần kêu
tracks.mood: a fault that turned into a home
tracks.subject: a ceiling fan that only rattles on speed three, so the family uses speed two for seven years
tracks.caption: Vietnamese funk cut live. Clavinet playing a syncopated riff through a light wah, drum kit recorded tight and dry with a cracking snare and busy hi-hat, electric bass played with a hard percussive thumb attack and mixed forward, two-piece horn section punching short stabs, electric guitar scratching sixteenths on the offbeats. Tight and dry with close drums and no reverb wash. Male voice, relaxed and conversational with light grit on line endings. 104 BPM, D minor. A fault that quietly turned into a home. No synth pad, no programmed drums, no autotune, no ballad section, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - clavinet and tight drums]

[Verse 1]
Cái quạt trần nhà tôi kêu, kêu từ năm hai nghìn mười tám
Cứ số ba thì kêu, số hai thì không
Nên cả nhà tôi bật số hai, suốt bảy năm
Nóng hơn một chút, nhưng không ai nói gì

[Chorus]
Cái quạt trần kêu
Ba tiếng kêu một vòng, tôi đếm được
Tôi ngủ được là nhờ nó, chứ không phải mặc kệ nó
Nhà này có một cái nhịp, và đó là nhịp

[Verse 2]
Thợ tới một lần, ổng nói "thay cái này là hết"
Hai trăm ngàn. Ba có tiền. Ba nói để coi.
Ba nói "để coi" đã bảy năm
Giờ tôi hiểu, ba không tiếc tiền, ba tiếc cái tiếng kêu đó

[Chorus]
Cái quạt trần kêu
Ba tiếng kêu một vòng, tôi vẫn đếm được
Tôi ngủ được là nhờ nó, chứ không phải mặc kệ nó
Nhà này có một cái nhịp, và đó vẫn là nhịp

[Bridge - bass only]
Tôi dọn ra riêng, phòng tôi im lắm
Im quá, tôi phải bật quạt số ba
Quạt mới. Không kêu. Tôi vẫn nằm nghe.

[Outro - clavinet, fading]
Về nhà cuối tuần
Số hai. Vẫn số hai.

tracks.title: bà bán xôi đầu hẻm
tracks.genre: contemporary Vietnamese folk with dan bau
tracks.mood: being known without being named
tracks.subject: twenty years of buying sticky rice from a woman who has never asked your name
tracks.caption: Contemporary Vietnamese folk. Dan bau monochord carrying the lead line with its whole-tone pitch bends and whistling harmonic tone left completely bare and unprocessed, sao truc bamboo flute answering with breathy ornaments, dan tranh zither plucked sparsely underneath, a soft frame drum keeping a slow pulse instead of a kit, upright bass very quiet. Sparse and dry with a lot of silence and no modern low end. Female voice, plain and conversational with traditional folk ornamentation only on the line endings. 86 BPM, G minor pentatonic. Being known without ever being named. No drum kit, no synth, no four-on-the-floor, no EDM production, no key change.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - dan bau and sao truc]

[Verse 1]
Năm giờ sáng, góc hẻm, cái mẹt, lá chuối, nồi xôi còn bốc khói
Bà ngồi đó từ trước khi tôi biết đi học
Hai mươi năm tôi mua, hai mươi năm bà không hỏi tên tôi
Bà chỉ nói "con ăn gì" — hai mươi năm, đúng ba chữ đó

[Pre-Chorus]
Nhưng bà nhớ tôi ăn xôi gấc
Và bà nhớ tôi không ăn hành

[Chorus]
Bà bán xôi đầu hẻm
Không biết tên tôi, nhưng biết tôi
Có một kiểu quen thuộc không cần tên
Và tôi sợ cái ngày tôi phải tự giới thiệu lại từ đầu

[Verse 2]
Tháng trước bà nghỉ ba ngày, cái góc đó trống, tôi thấy nó rộng ra
Tôi không biết hỏi ai, tôi không biết bà tên gì mà hỏi
Ngày thứ tư bà ra lại, chống gậy
Tôi mua hai gói. Bà nói "con ăn gì". Tôi mừng muốn khóc vì ba chữ đó.

[Chorus]
Bà bán xôi đầu hẻm
Không biết tên tôi, nhưng biết tôi
Có một kiểu quen thuộc không cần tên
Và tôi vẫn sợ cái ngày đó, nhưng hôm nay thì chưa

[Outro - dan bau alone]
Xôi gấc. Không hành.
Mai con lại ra.

tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - drum break and vinyl noise]

[Verse 1]
早上六點半 我站在一間我不想吃的店門口
第十四個 前面十三個都比我年輕
我幫一個不認識的人排隊 一小時兩百塊
接單的備註寫「限量 務必買到」

[Hook]
我幫你排隊
你睡到十點 我站到十點
這不丟臉 我真的不覺得丟臉
我只是第一次知道 原來時間可以這樣賣

[Verse 2]
排到的時候剩最後六份 我拿到了
我傳照片給他 他回一個讚
沒有說謝謝 也不用說
這是交易 我提醒我自己 這是一筆乾淨的交易

[Hook]
我幫你排隊
你睡到十點 我站到十點
這不丟臉 我真的不覺得丟臉
我只是第一次知道 原來時間可以這樣賣 而且賣得很便宜

[Bridge - bass and scratches only]
回家的公車上 我聞到袋子裡的味道
我沒有打開
那不是我的

[Outro - break stops]
明天七點 另外一家
我設了鬧鐘
